description.value: This study tested the stability and within-participants reliability of alcohol cue-elicited striatal BOLD activation across two fMRI scans separated by 14 days in non-treatment-seeking alcohol-dependent participants using hierarchical linear modeling.

spans.text: This study aimed to test the stability of alcohol cue-elicited fMRI striatal activation using HLM.

value: we hypothesized that visual alcohol cues would again elicit greater activation than control cues in anatomically and functionally defined regions of interest encompassing bilateral VS/DS.

we posited that the magnitude of cue-elicited activation in these ROIs would not change significantly between two scans separated by two weeks, and that within-participants activations would have good test–retest reliability.
